Export a panel as a 3D model file

Source: R/export-3d.R
export_3d.Rd

Write the scene of one panel to a file that 3D software opens: glTF binary (.glb) or glTF with a separate buffer (.gltf and .bin) for Blender and the web, PLY, OBJ with an MTL material file, or binary STL. Faces are triangulated, paths become tubes or line primitives, and points become small solids or point primitives, all in model coordinates: the panel box scaled by the aspect of coord_3d(), with its longest side size long.

Usage

export_3d(
  plot,
  file,
  panel = 1L,
  furniture = FALSE,
  lines = c("tube", "line"),
  points = c("mesh", "point"),
  size = 1,
  width = 640L,
  height = 640L,
  dpi = 96,
  print = NULL
)

Arguments

plot

A ggplot with coord_3d().

file

Output path. Its extension selects the format: .glb, .gltf, .ply, .obj, .stl or .3mf.

panel

Panel index in layout order, default 1.

furniture

Whether to include the panes, grid lines and box edges, default FALSE.

lines

"tube" (default) writes each path as a closed tube with the drawn line width as diameter; "line" writes line primitives.

points

"mesh" (default) writes each point as a solid of its drawn size: a cube for square shapes, a tetrahedron for triangles, an octahedron for diamonds and a sphere for the other shapes; "point" writes point primitives.

size

Length of the longest side of the box in file units, default 1.

width, height

Device size in pixels used to lay out the plot, default 640 each. Tubes and solids keep the size relative to the box that lines and points have in a plot of this size.

dpi

Device resolution, default 96 dots per inch.

print

Optional print_3d() specification for closed millimetre solids in STL or 3MF output.

Value

file, invisibly.

Details

glTF output follows the glTF 2.0 specification and is the route into Blender, whose importer reads its meshes, materials, cameras and animation. The vertical axis of the plot becomes +y. Each layer is one named node (layer1_point, layer2_surface, ...), and the furniture is a node furniture with the children panes, grid and box, so layers can be selected, hidden and restyled after import. Mapped colours are vertex colours (COLOR_0, linear light), so a colour scale needs no material per colour. Faces drawn with lighting (light_3d() and shade) use one lit material whose base colour multiplies the vertex colours; all other geometry uses the KHR_materials_unlit extension. Translucent geometry uses alpha blending and every material is double sided. A node camera holds the view of the panel, so the file opens on the plot's view; an oblique projection is written as an orthographic camera along the sight direction. animate_3d() writes animated glTF files.

PLY output is binary with vertex normals and 8-bit sRGB vertex colours; line primitives are edge elements. OBJ output writes one object per node, sRGB vertex colours after each vertex position, and one MTL material per distinct colour; its vertical axis is +y, as OBJ importers expect. PLY and STL keep the vertical axis of the plot as +z. STL holds triangles only, so it requires lines = "tube" and points = "mesh".

Ordinary model exports omit text and write dashed lines solid. Printing exports include extruded text according to print_3d().

See also

animate_3d() for animated glTF files.

Examples

d <- expand.grid(x = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 15), y = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 15))
d$z <- d$x * exp(-d$x^2 - d$y^2)
p <- ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z)) +
  geom_surface_3d(ggplot2::aes(fill = z)) + coord_3d()
glb <- export_3d(p, tempfile(fileext = ".glb"))
file.size(glb)
export_3d(p, tempfile(fileext = ".stl"), size = 50)
